questions.stem: A respiratory therapist walks with a patient while tracking saturation and activity tolerance. What is the purpose of this evaluation?
questions.rationale: The six-minute walk assessment helps characterize exercise tolerance and oxygen needs.

questions.stem: A confused patient repeatedly tries to pull at a line. What is the guiding principle before restraints?
questions.rationale: Restraints are a last resort after appropriate alternatives.

options.text: Try appropriate less-restrictive alternatives and assess the cause
Skip assessment if the patient is restless

questions.stem: A patient lives alone and uses oxygen at home. Which discharge question best identifies a safety concern?
questions.rationale: Home safety assessment should identify oxygen-related ignition risks.

options.text: “Does anyone smoke or use open flames where oxygen is stored?”

questions.stem: An ICU patient becomes agitated when alarms sound and several staff members speak simultaneously. Which initial change is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Reducing excessive stimuli addresses sensory overload.

options.text: Reduce unnecessary noise and coordinate communication
Keep the lights bright all night
Increase the number of simultaneous conversations

questions.stem: A patient asks to try relaxation before a dressing change. Which actions may support comfort without replacing indicated analgesia? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Breathing, imagery, and environment are complementary comfort interventions.

options.text: Cancel ordered pain medication without discussion

questions.stem: A tornado warning is announced. A bedbound patient is near a window. Which action follows the course guidance?
questions.rationale: Tornado precautions prioritize interior protection and distance from windows.

options.text: Move the bed away from windows and protect the patient as directed
Raise the window shade to watch the storm
Take the patient to an open balcony

questions.stem: A COPD patient has a prescription for an inhaled bronchodilator. Which finding best indicates therapeutic benefit?
questions.rationale: Improved airflow and reduced dyspnea suggest bronchodilator benefit.

questions.stem: An order is to infuse 600 mL over 5 hours using tubing calibrated at 15 gtt/mL. What is the drip rate to the nearest whole drop?
A patient describes sharp pain directly over a fresh incision that increases when the area is touched. How should the nurse document the location pattern?
questions.rationale: Pain centered at the injured site is localized rather than referred.

questions.stem: Match each safety term to its description.
questions.rationale: The course safety slides group these into three categories: near miss, patient safety event, and sentinel event (never event). Source: fundies safety.pdf, slide 6.

targets.text: Potential error intercepted before harm occurs
Unexpected event that occurs without patient injury
Unexpected adverse event resulting in death or serious harm

questions.stem: A patient received an opioid 20 minutes ago and is difficult to arouse with slow respirations. What is the priority?
questions.rationale: Respiratory depression and reduced responsiveness require immediate assessment and escalation.

options.text: Assess airway and breathing and activate the appropriate urgent response
Wait until the next pain assessment
Give another opioid for persistent pain

questions.stem: A child has an order for 80 mg of an oral liquid. The bottle reads 40 mg/5 mL. How many mL are required?
A patient receives a medication intended for another patient but has no apparent injury. Which statement is accurate?
questions.rationale: Errors reaching patients warrant assessment and reporting even without evident harm.

options.text: A patient safety event occurred and should be reported per policy
Nothing happened because injury is absent
It is always a sentinel event
Reporting is unnecessary if the patient is stable

questions.stem: A patient says, “I'll use petroleum jelly around my nose while wearing oxygen.” What teaching is needed?
questions.rationale: Avoid petroleum-based products near oxygen equipment.

options.text: Choose an oxygen-safe water-based product if appropriate
Smoking is safe at low oxygen flow
Open flames do not matter with nasal cannula

questions.stem: Which statements demonstrate appropriate patient participation in a pain plan? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Reporting changes, functional goals, and adjunct measures support individualized pain care.

options.text: “I will report new or changing pain.”
“I can tell you what pain level allows me to move.”
“I should let my family press my PCA button.”
“I can ask about nonmedication comfort measures.”

questions.stem: The order is 150 mg PO. Liquid medication contains 75 mg per 5 mL. How many mL are required?
A client weighs 54.5 kg. Convert to pounds using 2.2 lb/kg and round to the nearest tenth.
Which practices fit the categories discussed in class? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The course distinguishes mind–body, energy, manipulative, and biologically based approaches.

questions.stem: A patient with diminished foot sensation reports a new blister but no pain. What should the nurse infer?
questions.rationale: Loss of protective sensation can mask injury.

options.text: Absence of pain does not exclude tissue injury
The blister is harmless because it is painless
The patient is experiencing sensory overload
Pain medication must be administered before inspection

questions.stem: The nurse notices a frayed cord on an infusion pump before use. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Damaged electrical equipment must be removed from use and evaluated.

options.text: Remove the device from service and report it
Wrap it in tape and continue
Use it only when the floor is dry
Ask the patient to avoid touching it

questions.stem: A nurse catches an incorrect medication before it reaches the patient. How should the event be classified?
questions.rationale: An intercepted error that does not reach the patient is a near miss.

questions.stem: A patient practices guided imagery before a painful procedure. How should the nurse classify the technique?
questions.rationale: Guided imagery is a mind–body approach.

questions.stem: A patient with COPD becomes too short of breath to finish a sentence and appears newly confused. Which action has priority?
questions.rationale: Acute mental-status and respiratory changes may indicate serious deterioration.

options.text: Prompt respiratory assessment and escalation of care
Encourage the patient to walk alone

questions.stem: An order is for 500 mg PO. Tablets are labeled 250 mg each. How many tablets should the nurse give?
questions.rationale: 500 ÷ 250 = 2 tablets.

questions.stem: A COPD patient becomes breathless while bathing. What instruction supports energy conservation?
questions.rationale: Pacing and controlled breathing support activity tolerance.

options.text: Exhale during effort rather than holding breath

questions.stem: Before discharge, a patient who uses a walker says the bathroom has loose rugs. Which action is best?
questions.rationale: Home safety planning addresses environment and available support.

questions.stem: A patient is breathing rapidly during severe anxiety and reports tingling fingers. Which change is most consistent with hyperventilation?
questions.rationale: Hyperventilation increases CO₂ exhalation and may lower arterial CO₂.

questions.stem: An active shooter is nearby and no safe exit is available. What should staff do according to the course guidance?
questions.rationale: Hide and secure the location when evacuation is unsafe.

options.text: Hide out of sight, lock or barricade, and silence phones
Call out loudly to locate others
Leave the door open for visibility

questions.stem: Which findings suggest a sensory deficit rather than insufficient environmental stimulation? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Deficit means impaired reception or processing of sensory input, not simply lack of stimulation.

options.text: Reduced touch sensation in the toes

questions.stem: Match each oxygen-delivery device with its defining clinical use or requirement.
questions.rationale: The oxygen devices differ by flow, concentration control, and design.

targets.text: Low-flow oxygen with easy speaking and eating
Requires minimum flow to prevent CO₂ rebreathing

questions.stem: A patient reports receiving Reiki sessions. Which category does the course associate with Reiki?
questions.rationale: The lecture groups Reiki and healing touch with bioenergetic approaches.

questions.stem: An older adult with dementia grimaces and guards the abdomen during repositioning. Which approach is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Behavioral cues help assess pain when self-report is limited.

options.text: Assume no pain because the patient cannot rate it
Use a validated behavioral pain assessment and assess possible causes
Ask only the roommate about pain

questions.stem: A family member lights a candle in the room of a patient receiving oxygen. What should the nurse do first?
questions.rationale: Oxygen supports combustion; flames are unsafe around oxygen equipment.

options.text: Remove the ignition source and reinforce oxygen fire safety
Lower oxygen until the candle burns out
Ignore it if the oxygen is via nasal cannula

questions.stem: A client reports a dull ache in the right shoulder after a meal. The provider suspects gallbladder disease. Which explanation best accounts for the shoulder discomfort?
questions.rationale: Visceral pain can be perceived at a location distant from the involved organ.

options.text: Referred pain from a visceral source

questions.stem: A COPD patient reports thicker sputum, worsening cough, and greater dyspnea than usual. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Changes from baseline may indicate COPD exacerbation requiring evaluation.

options.text: Assess for an exacerbation and report changes promptly
Assume the findings are expected and ignore them

questions.stem: The nurse is setting up a Venturi mask. Which action is essential for ordered oxygen concentration?
questions.rationale: Venturi devices require the correct adapter and flow to deliver the selected FiO₂.

options.text: Use the correct adapter and prescribed flow settings
Use any flow rate without checking the device

questions.stem: A patient on nasal oxygen develops dry nasal mucosa. Which response is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Assess oxygen-related dryness and use oxygen-safe measures.

options.text: Check the oxygen equipment and prescribed settings
Apply petroleum jelly inside the nostrils

questions.stem: Which actions are consistent with tornado precautions? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Shelter in protected areas and follow facility guidance.

options.text: Move ambulatory patients toward designated protected interior areas
Use elevators routinely regardless of conditions

questions.stem: A patient with COPD exhales through pursed lips. What is the intended benefit?
questions.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing helps maintain airway pressure during exhalation.

options.text: Prolong exhalation and help reduce air trapping
Eliminate the need for all prescribed therapy
Stop air from leaving the lungs

questions.stem: A patient asks the nurse to demonstrate pursed-lip breathing. Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: The technique uses a slow, prolonged exhalation through pursed lips.

options.text: Inhale gently through the nose and exhale slowly through pursed lips
Inhale and exhale rapidly through the mouth
Hold the breath for as long as possible
Exhale forcefully with an open mouth

questions.stem: Match each communication or sensory condition to its defining characteristic.
questions.rationale: Communication and sensory concepts are distinguished by the primary deficit.

questions.stem: A patient declines to disclose an herbal supplement after feeling judged. Which response best restores therapeutic communication?
questions.rationale: Nonjudgmental inquiry supports a complete care history.

options.text: “I ask everyone because supplements can affect treatment; what do you take?”

questions.stem: An IM order is 30 mg. A vial contains 50 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse draw up?
A patient with COPD asks why stopping smoking matters despite established lung disease. What should the nurse emphasize?
questions.rationale: Smoking cessation remains important for COPD.

options.text: Avoiding smoke can reduce further lung injury
Stopping has no benefit with established COPD
Smoking is safe near oxygen if the flow is low

questions.stem: Which question is most likely to elicit an accurate complementary-therapy history?
questions.rationale: Open, nonjudgmental questioning encourages disclosure.

options.text: “You don't take any unapproved remedies, do you?”
“What vitamins, supplements, herbs, or other therapies do you use?”

questions.stem: A patient has lower-back pain that travels down one leg. Which assessment detail is most important to clarify the pattern?
questions.rationale: Location and radiation help characterize pain and guide follow-up.

options.text: Whether pain radiates and where it travels

questions.stem: A patient asks whether acupuncture should replace prescribed treatment for an acute infection. Which response is safest?
questions.rationale: Complementary therapies should not automatically displace indicated medical treatment.

options.text: “Let's discuss complementary options with the team without stopping prescribed treatment.”
“There is no reason to tell the provider.”

questions.stem: A patient with expressive aphasia points to a body diagram but cannot name the painful area. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Alternative communication methods support assessment when speech is impaired.

options.text: Use the picture board and yes/no questions to clarify needs

questions.stem: An older adult becomes dizzy when standing and has fallen twice recently. Which interventions reduce fall risk? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Environmental precautions and appropriate assistance reduce fall risk.

options.text: Keep the bed low and locked
Place the call light within reach

questions.stem: A hospitalized patient with intact hearing and vision has spent days alone with little conversation and reports feeling disconnected. Which problem is most likely?
questions.rationale: Insufficient meaningful stimulation can cause sensory deprivation even with intact senses.

questions.stem: After a prescribed analgesic, the patient reports pain decreased from 8/10 to 4/10 but still cannot transfer to the chair. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Evaluation includes whether the functional goal was achieved, not only the numeric score.

options.text: Reassess function and collaborate on additional safe pain management
Tell the patient to ignore the pain

questions.stem: Which patient change should prompt immediate reassessment of oxygen delivery?
questions.rationale: Restlessness and increased work of breathing can signal worsening oxygenation.

options.text: New restlessness and increased work of breathing

questions.stem: The nurse learns a patient cannot safely climb stairs at home after hospitalization. Which collaboration is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: Mobility assessment and discharge planning require relevant disciplines.

questions.stem: A nurse finds a simple face mask running at a flow lower than the device's recommended minimum. What is the concern?
questions.rationale: Insufficient flow through a simple mask can allow CO₂ rebreathing.

options.text: The mask becomes a Venturi device
The patient receives no humidification only

questions.stem: Which changes in a COPD patient's condition require follow-up? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Worsening dyspnea, wheezing, and edema warrant assessment.

questions.stem: A patient with hearing impairment keeps asking the nurse to repeat instructions. Which approach supports understanding?
questions.rationale: Face-to-face communication and comprehension checks improve teaching.

options.text: Cover the mouth to reduce distractions

questions.stem: A patient cannot afford prescribed medicines and reports unstable housing. Which referral is most helpful?
questions.rationale: Interprofessional referral helps address social and discharge needs.

questions.stem: The nurse sees smoke entering a hallway from a closed room. Which RACE action helps limit spread while the response is activated?
questions.rationale: Closing doors helps contain fire and smoke.

options.text: Keep fire doors closed and contain the area

questions.stem: A patient on home oxygen asks where to store a backup cylinder. Which response is best?
questions.rationale: Oxygen cylinders must be secured and protected from heat and ignition sources.

options.text: Secure it upright away from heat and open flames
Place it next to a gas stove
Keep it unsecured on the couch
Store it next to smoking materials

questions.stem: A patient with a tracheostomy has audible secretions and difficulty moving air. What should the nurse prioritize?
questions.rationale: Tracheostomy care prioritizes a patent airway and management of secretions.

options.text: Assess airway patency and provide indicated suctioning with appropriate equipment

questions.stem: A patient has a respiratory rate of 8/min after receiving a sedative. Which findings are consistent with hypoventilation? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Hypoventilation reduces CO₂ elimination and may depress consciousness.

questions.stem: Which changes suggest a COPD patient has learned a useful breathing technique? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing slows exhalation and helps manage air trapping.

options.text: Uses rapid panting to empty lungs

questions.stem: After receiving a sedating medication, a patient breathes 7 times per minute and becomes drowsy. Which concern is most urgent?
questions.rationale: Markedly reduced ventilation can retain CO₂ and impair oxygenation.

questions.stem: After a stroke, a patient understands a request to raise an arm but speaks in short, effortful phrases. Which impairment is most likely?
questions.rationale: Expressive aphasia impairs production of language while comprehension may be preserved.

questions.stem: An active shooter is reported and a safe exit is available. Which actions follow the course guidance? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Run if a safe path exists; leave belongings and avoid exposing others.

options.text: Warn others away from the danger if possible

questions.stem: A unit reviews a wrong-site procedure that caused serious harm. What should the nurse recognize?
questions.rationale: Wrong-site procedures are serious preventable safety events.

options.text: A serious reportable safety event requiring organizational response
An expected complication requiring no review

questions.stem: An IV infusion contains 720 mL to run over 8 hours. What pump rate is needed?
A patient reports burning, electric-shock sensations in both feet. Which pain quality is most consistent with this description?
questions.rationale: Burning and electric sensations suggest nerve-related pain.

questions.stem: A 500 mL IV bag must infuse over 4 hours. The drop factor is 12 gtt/mL. What is the drip rate to the nearest whole drop?
A patient is overwhelmed by frequent care interruptions. Which nursing plan best balances safety and stimulation?
questions.rationale: Coordinating care can reduce overload without compromising monitoring.

options.text: Cluster nonurgent care while maintaining required assessments
Keep multiple staff talking during procedures

questions.stem: During tracheostomy care, which finding demands the most immediate action?
questions.rationale: An obstructed airway is an immediate priority.

options.text: Sudden inability to pass air through the tube

questions.stem: A patient begins a generalized seizure in bed. What should the nurse do first?
questions.rationale: Protect, time, and position the patient; do not restrain or place objects in the mouth.

options.text: Turn the patient to the side when feasible

questions.stem: A patient weighs 68 kg. Using 2.2 lb/kg, what is the weight in pounds to the nearest tenth?
Match the fire response steps with the RACE sequence.
questions.rationale: RACE organizes the immediate fire response.

targets.text: Activate the alarm and report location
Close doors to limit smoke and fire
Use extinguisher if safe or evacuate

questions.stem: A deteriorating patient requires high-concentration oxygen while the team evaluates the cause. Which device has a reservoir bag and one-way valves?
questions.rationale: A nonrebreather is designed for high-concentration oxygen delivery.

questions.stem: The nurse finds the call bell on the floor and the patient's walker across the room. What should be corrected first?
questions.rationale: Accessible assistance and mobility equipment are basic fall precautions.

options.text: Restore access to the call bell and mobility aid before leaving
Ask the patient to retrieve both items
Raise the bed to maximum height

questions.stem: A restless patient is at risk of pulling out a line. Which sequence reflects least-restrictive care?
questions.rationale: Restraints require a safety-driven, least-restrictive approach.

options.text: Assess cause, try alternatives, reassess, then follow restraint policy only if necessary
Ask family to authorize any restraint without policy

questions.stem: A patient must receive 1,000 mL over 10 hours. What rate should the nurse set on the IV pump?
A patient says, “I didn't mention my tea because it isn't a medication.” Which nursing response is best?
questions.rationale: A nonjudgmental explanation supports safe disclosure.

options.text: “Herbal preparations can affect care; please tell us what you use.”
“Only prescription labels belong on the medication list.”

questions.stem: A COPD patient says, “I avoid drinking fluids because mucus is hard to cough up.” Which response is appropriate if fluids are not restricted?
questions.rationale: Adequate hydration can support secretion clearance when not contraindicated.

options.text: Encourage appropriate hydration to help keep secretions manageable
Recommend severe fluid restriction without an order
Tell the patient to suppress every cough

questions.stem: A family member says, “She is sleeping; I'll press her PCA button when she looks uncomfortable.” What is the nurse's best response?
questions.rationale: Only the patient activates a PCA button; proxy dosing can cause oversedation.

options.text: Explain that only the patient should activate the PCA dose button
Disconnect the PCA without assessing pain
Increase the basal rate without an order

questions.stem: A patient has an active seizure lasting several minutes without stopping. Which action is most important?
questions.rationale: Prolonged seizures can be an emergency and require prompt response.

options.text: Activate urgent help according to protocol and maintain airway safety
Put an object in the mouth
Leave the patient alone to recover

questions.stem: The nurse learns a patient uses herbal products with prescribed medicines. What is the best next step?
questions.rationale: A complete medication history includes supplements.

options.text: Document products and communicate possible interactions

questions.stem: A provider orders 45 mg IM. The medication concentration is 75 mg/mL. How many mL should be prepared?
Which details belong in restraint documentation? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Documentation covers indication, alternatives, monitoring, and response.

options.text: Only the color of the restraint

questions.stem: The nurse notices the PCA pump's medication label does not match the active order. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: An unresolved medication mismatch requires verification before administration.

options.text: Start the pump because it was delivered by pharmacy
Stop and resolve the discrepancy before administration
Change the order to match the label
Ask the patient which drug was intended

questions.stem: Which observations should the nurse include when comparing a COPD patient's current status with baseline? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Respiratory effort, secretions, saturation, and mentation help detect deterioration.

questions.stem: The nurse is teaching a patient who reads lips. Which actions support communication? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Visibility, reduced noise, and confirmation of understanding improve communication.

options.text: Maintain eye contact and face the patient

questions.stem: A COPD patient leans forward with hands supported during dyspnea. What is the nurse's best action?
questions.rationale: Upright supported positioning may ease breathing while assessment continues.

options.text: Support a position of comfort and assess respiratory effort
Force the patient to lie flat

questions.stem: A small fire starts in a patient room. A patient is in immediate danger. According to RACE, what is the first priority if it can be done safely?
questions.rationale: RACE begins with rescue, followed by alarm, containment, and extinguish/evacuate.

questions.stem: A patient asks for meditation to help anxiety while receiving standard treatment. What outcome should the nurse evaluate?
questions.rationale: Integrative interventions should be evaluated against patient-centered goals.

options.text: The patient's reported anxiety and ability to participate in care
Whether the patient stops all medicines
Whether vital signs are no longer necessary

questions.stem: A patient requests massage in addition to prescribed care. What is the best interpretation of integrative care?
questions.rationale: Integrative care uses complementary measures alongside appropriate conventional treatment.

options.text: Combining appropriate conventional and complementary approaches

questions.stem: A client with peripheral neuropathy cannot detect a hot heating pad against the feet. What is the priority teaching?
questions.rationale: Reduced protective sensation increases burn and injury risk.

options.text: Test water and device temperatures with unaffected skin or assistance
Use a hotter pad to restore sensation

questions.stem: A patient needs low-flow supplemental oxygen and can eat and speak without a mask. Which device is commonly appropriate?
questions.rationale: A nasal cannula provides low-flow oxygen while allowing eating and conversation.

options.text: Tracheostomy collar for a patient without a tracheostomy

questions.stem: Match each therapy with the category emphasized in the course.
questions.rationale: These are the therapy categories discussed in the lecture.

questions.stem: A patient rates pain 6/10 but says, “I need to be comfortable enough to cough and walk.” Which goal is most useful?
questions.rationale: A functional pain goal links relief to necessary activity.

options.text: Pain at a tolerable level that permits coughing and walking

questions.stem: A prescription calls for 375 mg PO. Tablets are 125 mg each. How many tablets should be administered?
questions.rationale: 375 ÷ 125 = 3 tablets.

questions.stem: Match the event with the most accurate safety classification.
questions.rationale: Event classification guides reporting and systems improvement.

pairs.prompt: Unexpected death related to serious care failure

questions.stem: Before starting a PCA pump, which action addresses a preventable medication error?
questions.rationale: An independent verification supports PCA safety.

options.text: Verify the medication and settings using the required independent check
Ask the patient to program the prescription

questions.stem: An alert postoperative adult says, “I have pain, but I cannot put a number on it.” What should the nurse do first?
questions.rationale: Pain is subjective; use patient report and an assessment method the patient can understand.

options.text: Ask the patient to describe the pain and offer an appropriate alternative scale
Give the maximum available opioid dose
Ask a family member to choose the rating

questions.stem: During morning rounds, a client is hard of hearing. Which communication approach is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Facing the patient, speaking clearly and using a lower tone improves comprehension.

options.text: Face the client and speak clearly in a lower-pitched voice.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, a patient is discharged with home oxygen. Which statement shows correct understanding?
questions.rationale: Oxygen safety includes no smoking/open flames, heat avoidance, and securing cylinders.

options.text: Keep oxygen equipment away from flames and secure cylinders upright.
Smoke only when oxygen is at a low setting.
Store cylinders unsecured on their sides.
Use petroleum jelly on oxygen tubing.

questions.stem: A patient admitted with dehydration is prescribed 625 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride to infuse over 6 hours. The IV pump is functioning normally. What rate in mL/hr should the nurse program? Round to the nearest tenth.
questions.rationale: Divide 625 mL by 6 hours = 104.166..., rounded to 104.2 mL/hr.

questions.stem: Which actions align with active shooter safety guidance? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The lecture teaches run, hide, fight according to the situation.

options.text: Evacuate through a clear safe exit when possible
Remain in open view to record video

questions.stem: During morning rounds, a stroke survivor says only a few words but follows directions. How can the nurse assess needs?
questions.rationale: The instructor recommends yes/no questions and picture boards.

options.text: Yes/no questions and a picture communication board

questions.stem: Which findings or conditions are associated with sensory overload? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Excessive uncontrolled stimuli can cause sensory overload.

options.text: Agitation from excessive alarms and bright lights
Boredom in a quiet isolated room
Loss of touch sensation from neuropathy

questions.stem: During morning rounds, the nurse teaches breathing through pursed lips with a longer exhalation. What is the purpose?
questions.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing slows exhalation and helps release trapped air.

options.text: Breathing only through the mouth rapidly

questions.stem: During morning rounds, during a generalized seizure, which nursing intervention protects the patient?
questions.rationale: Seizure precautions include positioning, timing, and injury prevention; do not restrain or insert objects.

options.text: Turn the patient to the side and time the seizure.
Insert a tongue blade into the mouth.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, the client receives Reiki. Which complementary therapy category applies?
questions.rationale: The instructor groups Reiki and healing touch with bioenergetic approaches.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, which exposure is an important COPD risk factor?
questions.rationale: Tobacco use is a major COPD risk factor.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, a confused patient is pulling at a necessary device. When may restraints be considered?
questions.rationale: Restraints are a last resort; assess alternatives, safety, and orders.

options.text: Use only as a last resort after less restrictive options.
Use as punishment for calling frequently.

questions.stem: A postoperative patient is prescribed 150 mg of a medication by mouth. The medication is supplied as scored 75 mg tablets. How many tablets should the nurse administer?
questions.rationale: 150 mg ÷ 75 mg per tablet = 2 tablets.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, a client with diabetic peripheral neuropathy cannot reliably feel foot injuries. Which sense is affected?
questions.rationale: Peripheral neuropathy may reduce the ability to sense touch.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, which nonpharmacologic technique is appropriate during COPD breathlessness?
questions.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing helps manage trapped air and dyspnea.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, which charting best supports appropriate restraint care?
questions.rationale: Document indication, attempted alternatives, monitoring, and patient response.

options.text: Behavior, unsuccessful alternatives, assessments, and response.
Only the nurse’s opinion of the patient
No documentation if a provider orders them

questions.stem: During morning rounds, a client with gallbladder disease reports discomfort in the right shoulder. Which pain pattern is this?
questions.rationale: Referred pain is perceived away from its source; the lecture uses gallbladder pain in the shoulder.

questions.stem: Which statements accurately distinguish acute and chronic pain? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The instructor distinguishes acute protective pain from chronic pain that may persist without a protective purpose.

options.text: Acute pain can serve as a protective warning.
Chronic pain may persist without a protective function.
Chronic pain always indicates new tissue injury.
Acute pain never alerts a person to injury.
Chronic pain is always visible on imaging.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, the nurse sees flames next to a patient. What is the first RACE step?
questions.rationale: RACE begins with rescue, then alarm, contain, and extinguish/evacuate as appropriate.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, a patient asks about chiropractic care. Which category of complementary therapy is this?
questions.rationale: Chiropractic care is a manual/body-based approach.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, the client says “pain, leg, bad” but understands the nurse. What is the likely communication impairment?
questions.rationale: Expressive aphasia impairs word production while comprehension may remain.

questions.stem: Which findings can accompany COPD and warrant nursing assessment? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The lecture lists wheezing, dyspnea, fatigue, and swelling among COPD manifestations.

questions.stem: During morning rounds, an alert adult describes postoperative pain clearly. Which pain scale should the nurse select?
questions.rationale: The instructor recommends the 0–10 scale for verbally communicative, developmentally appropriate adults.

questions.stem: Which changes can suggest a COPD exacerbation? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Changes in dyspnea, cough, and sputum suggest an exacerbation.

options.text: Improving activity tolerance without new symptoms

questions.stem: During morning rounds, which referral addresses medication affordability and housing instability?
questions.rationale: Interprofessional collaboration and early referral address social needs.

questions.stem: Which statements about a simple oxygen mask are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Simple masks generally require 5–10 L/min to avoid CO₂ retention.

options.text: It commonly uses a flow rate of 5–10 L/min
Too little flow can promote CO₂ rebreathing
A flow of 1 L/min is standard
It delivers an exact fixed FiO₂ like a Venturi mask
It is identical to a nasal cannula

questions.stem: A patient recovering from surgery needs 675 mL of IV fluid infused over 7 hours. The pump is unavailable; the gravity tubing has a drop factor of 10 gtt/mL. At how many gtt/min should the nurse regulate the infusion? Round to the nearest whole drop.
questions.rationale: (675 mL × 10 gtt/mL) ÷ (7 × 60 minutes) = 16.07 gtt/min, rounded to 16 gtt/min.

questions.stem: Match each clinical concept to its best description.
questions.rationale: Match each concept with its accurate description; review the listed source for definitions and safety applications.

targets.text: Serious preventable event from the designated list

questions.stem: Which comfort measures can complement prescribed pain management? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: The instructor identifies mind–body techniques as complementary options rather than replacements for indicated care.

options.text: Withhold prescribed analgesics without discussing it
Explain that all pain is imaginary

questions.stem: A patient with difficulty swallowing tablets is prescribed 200 mg of an oral liquid medication. The bottle reads 40 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should the nurse administer?
A patient being treated for an infection has an order for 30 mg of a medication IM. The vial is labeled 50 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse draw into the syringe?
questions.rationale: 30 mg ÷ 50 mg/mL = 0.6 mL.

Into elevators regardless of facility policy

questions.stem: The nurse prepares a prescribed oral liquid medication. The provider orders 340 mg PO. The liquid label reads 50 mg/5 mL. How many mL should be administered?
On the nursing unit, a patient begins having a seizure in bed. Which action is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Seizure precautions include positioning, timing, and injury prevention; do not restrain or insert objects.

options.text: Turn the patient to the side and time the seizure.
Insert a tongue blade into the mouth.

questions.stem: The nurse checks a prescribed oral medication against the unit-dose package. The order is 375 mg PO. Tablets contain 125 mg each. How many tablets will the nurse administer? Assume the prescribed dose is appropriate and administer whole tablets only.
questions.rationale: 375 mg ordered ÷ 125 mg per tablet = 3 whole tablets. Verify the order and medication before administration.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, a stroke survivor understands questions but can only say short, effortful phrases. Which aphasia fits?
questions.rationale: Expressive aphasia impairs word production while comprehension may remain.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, a dyspneic COPD client is anxious and tripoding. Which nursing intervention can assist ventilation?
questions.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing helps manage trapped air and dyspnea.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, the nurse explains care to a patient with hearing impairment. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Facing the patient, speaking clearly and using a lower tone improves comprehension.

options.text: Face the client and speak clearly in a lower-pitched voice.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, a patient is receiving IV morphine. Which assessment takes priority?
questions.rationale: Opioids may depress respirations; monitor ventilation and sedation.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, the provider orders a precise fixed inspired oxygen concentration. Which device should the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: A Venturi mask delivers a precise fixed oxygen concentration.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, a patient reports reduced touch sensation in both feet. Which alteration should the nurse identify?
questions.rationale: Peripheral neuropathy may reduce the ability to sense touch.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, which type of therapy includes manual body manipulation?
questions.rationale: Chiropractic care is a manual/body-based approach.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, which intervention is categorized as a biologically based complementary therapy?
questions.rationale: The instructor classifies herbs and aromatherapy as biologically based therapies.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, a COPD patient feels short of breath. Which technique helps release trapped air?
questions.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing slows exhalation and helps release trapped air.

options.text: Breathing only through the mouth rapidly

questions.stem: A patient has a prescribed IV fluid infusion. An IV pump must infuse 1500 mL over 5 hours. What rate in mL/hr should be programmed (nearest tenth)?
On the nursing unit, which intervention is part of routine tracheostomy management?
questions.rationale: Tracheostomy care maintains a patent airway and requires appropriate suctioning equipment.

options.text: Maintain prescribed stoma and inner-cannula care.
Leave a blocked inner cannula untouched.
Use suction without the required equipment.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, the nurse is starting PCA therapy. Which practice supports safe administration?
questions.rationale: The instructor emphasizes second-RN checks and safe PCA setup.

options.text: Verify pump initiation and changes with a second RN per protocol.
Allow family members to press the button.
Assume an opioid cannot cause sedation.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, a patient with impaired mobility is being discharged. Which assessment is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Home safety education considers the patient’s condition, living environment, and support.

options.text: Assess environmental hazards and support needs.
Assume the home has no fall risks.
Do not ask about available caregivers.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, which approach is considered a bioenergetic therapy in the lecture?
questions.rationale: The instructor groups Reiki and healing touch with bioenergetic approaches.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, which oxygen delivery device commonly provides 1–6 L/min by nasal prongs?
questions.rationale: A standard nasal cannula provides low-flow oxygen, generally 1–6 L/min.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, which teaching point is essential for home oxygen safety?
questions.rationale: Oxygen safety includes no smoking/open flames, heat avoidance, and securing cylinders.

options.text: Keep oxygen equipment away from flames and secure cylinders upright.
Smoke only when oxygen is at a low setting.
Store cylinders unsecured on their sides.
Use petroleum jelly on oxygen tubing.

questions.stem: On the nursing unit, a fully oriented adult can verbally rate pain. Which assessment tool is most appropriate?
questions.rationale: The instructor recommends the 0–10 scale for verbally communicative, developmentally appropriate adults.

questions.stem: The nurse needs to document the patient’s weight in pounds for a clinical calculation. A client weighs 74.6 kg. Convert the weight to pounds (nearest tenth). Use 1 kg = 2.2 lb.
On the nursing unit, a client has unstable housing and cannot afford prescriptions. Which team resource is appropriate?
questions.rationale: Interprofessional collaboration and early referral address social needs.
